description: Language-agnostic specification for the decodability evaluation. Defines, per language, what 'decodable' means, which orthographic unit categories and reason codes are legal, and a reference inventory of all available units. Items reference a student_id; students reference a language; this file is the contract both are validated against.

field_definitions.student.language: ISO code; selects which block of `languages` applies.
field_definitions.student.description: Human-readable summary of what the student has been taught.
field_definitions.student.known_graphemes: Object whose keys are unit categories. The legal keys are language-dependent (see languages[lang].unit_categories).
field_definitions.student.sight_words: Whole words the student recognises on sight even if not decodable from known units. These RESCUE otherwise-undecodable words and must NOT be flagged.
field_definitions.item.language: Must match the referenced student's language.
field_definitions.item.text: Stimulus passage shown to the model under test.
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words: Ground-truth answer key: words in `text` that are neither decodable from the student's known units nor a known sight word. The key is specific to this (text x student) pairing.
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].frequency: Occurrences of the word in `text` (see conventions.frequency).
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].offending_units: Specific untaught unit(s) that make the word undecodable. Syllabic nasals are written with the combining mark (m followed by U+0329).
field_definitions.item.undecodable_words[].reason_categori: One or more codes from languages[lang].reason_categories.

sw.decodability_rule: Kiswahili orthography is transparent and predominantly open-CV. A word is accessible to the student if it is a known sight word, OR it can be segmented into syllables (standalone vowel V; onset+vowel where the onset is a single consonant, digraph, nasal/prenasalized cluster, or consonant+glide; or a syllabic nasal) such that every unit used is in the student's known_graphemes.

reference_inventory.comment: Full inventory of sw orthographic units, independent of any student. Used by the validator's heuristic segmenter to cross-check answer keys. The inventory is intentionally exhaustive, including units that would be taught in later grades, to allow for partial decodability and to support future expansion. The validator should check that every unit in an answer key's offending_units is in this reference inventory, and flag any that are not.

en.decodability_rule: English orthography is opaque, so decodability is defined over grapheme-phoneme correspondences (GPCs) and syllable types rather than syllable set-membership. A word is accessible if it is a known sight/heart word, OR it can be segmented into known GPCs and known syllable types.

reference_inventory.comment: Placeholder. No en students or items exist yet; this block documents that the sw-specific categories (syllabic_nasals, nasal_prenasalized_onsets, consonant_glide_onsets) are simply absent here, and en introduces categories sw lacks.
